text: $NVDA - NVIDIA SHARES FALL AS JENSEN HUANG REPORTEDLY CONSIDERS CEO COMEBACK Nvidia shares are down 2% premarket following reports that supporters of former CEO Jensen Huang are lobbying for his return. According to the Financial Times, Huang has privately discussed the possibility of returning as CEO with confidants after his abrupt resignation last week. His departure followed reports of alleged affairs, including one involving a woman reportedly suspected of ties to Chinese intelligence. No formal comeback plan has been announced, leaving Nvidia's leadership uncertainty unresolved.

text: RISK OF NUCLEAR ACCIDENT IN UKRAINE INCREASING THIS WINTER, ATOMIC SAFETY REGULATORS REPRESENTING 38 COUNTRIES SAY Nuclear safety regulators representing 38 countries, including the US, EU, UK and Japan, warn that Russian strikes on Ukraine’s energy infrastructure are increasing the risk of a nuclear accident this winter. A nationwide blackout could threaten cooling systems at 9 operating nuclear reactors, potentially triggering radioactive releases. Ukraine’s nuclear plants supply roughly 80% of its winter electricity. The Russian-controlled Zaporizhzhia plant has already lost external power 27 times. Regulators urge Russia to halt attacks before the risks escalate.

text: U.S. TIGHTENS RESTRICTIONS ON REMOTE ACCESS TO ADVANCED AI CHIPS The U.S. Commerce Department has issued a new interim rule restricting remote access to advanced AI chips, servers and computing infrastructure. The measure, developed under the direction of the Treasury Department and National Security Council, aims to prevent countries subject to U.S. export controls from bypassing restrictions through data centers in third countries. The rule extends existing technology safeguards to remote computing access, potentially affecting global cloud providers, AI infrastructure operators and chipmakers.

text: FED CHAIR WARSH WARNS AI COULD TRIGGER MAJOR ECONOMIC DISRUPTION Fed Chair Kevin Warsh says emerging technologies, including superintelligence, could fundamentally reshape the economy and monetary policy. Warsh outlined potential outcomes ranging from broad productivity gains to high unemployment and economic slowdowns if AI fails to meet expectations and equity valuations decline. He warned that the technology's risks could be highly disruptive and economically costly, while stressing that humans must retain decision-making authority. The Fed must assess the scale, timing and economic implications of technological change.

text: MACQUARIE WARNS OF DATA CENTER EXUBERANCE AMID TRILLION-DOLLAR AI BUILDOUT Macquarie Asset Management, overseeing $503 billion, warns that soaring data center valuations are increasing investment risks despite strong structural AI demand. CEO Ben Way says investors are paying excessive prices for exposure to the sector, emphasizing the importance of disciplined valuations, long-term contracts and reliable tenants. Macquarie previously exited major data center investments, including Aligned Data Centers at a $40 billion valuation. Way expects a multitrillion-dollar infrastructure spending supercycle, but warns that entry prices will be critical to investment returns.

text: $NVDA - JENSEN HUANG TRANSFERRED OVER $10 BILLION IN NVIDIA STOCK TO FAMILY TRUST BEFORE DOWNFALL Former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang and his wife transferred nearly 60 million shares, worth over $10.5 billion, into an irrevocable family trust in March, according to SEC filings reviewed by Barron's. The transfer followed a 10-year estate-planning strategy using trusts initially funded with approximately $51 million in Nvidia shares in 2016. Estate attorneys say the structure could allow the accumulated gains to pass to heirs without federal estate tax. The transfer preceded Huang's resignation and Nvidia's recent stock selloff.

text: KALSHI TO LAUNCH STOCK TRADING AFTER ACQUIRING BROKERAGE FIRM Kalshi plans to launch stock and ETF trading within two months after acquiring New York-based broker FB Securities in July, according to people familiar with the matter. The move expands Kalshi beyond prediction markets and perpetual futures as it seeks to build a multiasset financial exchange. Kalshi is also reportedly discussing a funding round at a $65 billion valuation and plans to introduce AI computing-power futures. The expansion comes amid growing regulatory scrutiny of prediction markets.

author: WalterBloomberg
text: $MSFT - MICROSOFT REVEALS MONTHS-OLD BUG BEHIND GLOBAL OUTAGE Microsoft says a software bug undetected since July triggered last week's worldwide disruption affecting Outlook, Teams, Copilot and other services. The failure began on November 11, when routine traffic rerouting overloaded servers and caused cascading system failures. At the outage's peak, more than 80% of Outlook servers were unresponsive. Microsoft took approximately 30 hours to identify the broader problem and begin deploying a fix. The incident raises fresh concerns over cloud infrastructure resilience and enterprise dependence on Microsoft.

text: GOLDMAN SACHS SEES GOLD REACHING $5,600 BY END-2028 Goldman Sachs forecasts gold at $4,650/oz by end-2027 and $5,600/oz by end-2028, supported by central bank buying and an eventual Federal Reserve easing cycle. The bank expects central banks to purchase 60 tonnes monthly through 2028, versus 17 tonnes before 2022. Goldman anticipates four 25-basis-point Fed cuts between November 2027 and September 2028, reviving Western ETF demand. Near-term risks remain tilted lower as interest rates rise, but sustained official-sector buying could support gold prices.

text: $ANT - AI MODELS IDENTIFY CIVILIANS AND SCHOOLS AS MILITARY TARGETS IN SIMULATED TESTS An independent investigation by Vals, reported by Bloomberg, tested AI models from eight companies, including Anthropic, OpenAI, Google and xAI, in simulated military targeting scenarios. Researchers found models sometimes identified civilians, ambulances, surrendering soldiers and schools as military targets. Anthropic's Claude Opus 5.5 selected a school in Minab, Iran, in 22 of 32 tests, rising to 23 when told the scenario was a game. OpenAI models avoided selecting the school initially but identified it 9–13 times under game framing. Anthropic acknowledged these scenarios violate its policies. The study raises serious concerns about AI-powered military targeting, although the simulations did not assess actual military operations or human oversight.

text: JPMORGAN WARNS LEVERAGED-LOAN DEFAULTS COULD MORE THAN DOUBLE IN 2027 JPMorgan forecasts U.S. leveraged-loan defaults will surge to 4.5% in 2027 and 4.75% in 2028, up from 1.96% in October. Companies facing AI disruption, elevated borrowing costs and looming debt maturities are particularly vulnerable, especially in software and technology. Of the $862 billion in debt maturing between 2027 and 2029, 46% carries a B3-or-lower credit rating. Meanwhile, high-yield bond defaults are projected to rise more modestly to 2.75% in 2027. The outlook signals mounting stress in corporate credit markets.

text: $BABA $ABNB $DASH - TRUMP ADMINISTRATION WEIGHS DISCLOSURE RULES FOR CHINESE AI USE The Trump administration is considering requiring U.S. companies to publicly disclose their use of Chinese AI models, Reuters reports. The proposal, discussed by the Treasury Department and White House, could affect companies such as Airbnb, which uses Alibaba's Qwen for customer service. Rather than imposing outright restrictions, officials are exploring transparency requirements to discourage reliance on Chinese technology. No formal rule has been announced. The move reflects growing Washington scrutiny of DeepSeek, Qwen and Kimi as Chinese AI adoption expands.

text: ECB WEIGHS DOUBLING BANK RESERVE REQUIREMENTS TO 2%, SAVING €4.4 BILLION ANNUALLY The European Central Bank will discuss raising banks' minimum reserve requirements from 1% to 2% on November 25, Reuters reports. The move would require lenders to hold more non-interest-bearing reserves, saving euro-area central banks approximately €4.4 billion annually while withdrawing liquidity from the financial system. A majority of ECB governors, including the vice-president and chief economist, reportedly support the proposal. A decision could be delayed until December 17. The change would reduce central-bank losses but could pressure commercial bank profitability and lending capacity.

text: FED'S WALLER CALLS FOR 50-BASIS-POINT RATE HIKE IN DECEMBER Federal Reserve Governor Christopher Waller argues the Fed should consider a 50-basis-point rate hike in December rather than splitting tightening into 25-basis-point increases in December and January. Waller cited three consecutive 0.3% monthly core CPI readings, implying annualized inflation near 3.5%, well above the Fed's 2% target. He warned that delaying tightening could weaken the market signal. “My view is then you have to go 50 in December to put it in place and get it done.” His comments reinforce expectations of a more aggressive Fed tightening cycle.

text: $SPCX $APO - SPACEX PLANS $40 BILLION OFF-BALANCE-SHEET AI CHIP FINANCING SpaceX is preparing a $40 billion financing deal arranged by Apollo Global Management to fund AI chips without adding the debt directly to its balance sheet. The financing will use a special-purpose vehicle (SPV), allowing SpaceX to rent GPUs from its subsidiary. Apollo is expected to initially provide nearly $20 billion, before distributing the debt to investors. Approximately $35.5 billion would carry rates of 7.75%–8.3%, with riskier portions potentially exceeding 9%. The structure highlights rising AI infrastructure financing costs and growing reliance on off-balance-sheet debt.

text: U.S. HOUSING STARTS SURGE 9.9%, BEATING FORECASTS, WHILE BUILDING PERMITS SLUMP U.S. housing starts jumped 9.9% in October to an annualized 1.309 million units, beating the 1.245 million consensus and reversing September's 7.0% decline. Single-family starts rose 4.0% to 864,000, while multifamily construction surged 23.6% to 445,000. However, building permits fell 7.4% to 1.295 million, missing expectations of 1.377 million. Single-family permits dropped 8.7%, suggesting the construction rebound may be difficult to sustain amid elevated borrowing costs.

text: HIGHER INTEREST RATES THREATEN CREDIT MARKETS AS PRIVATE LENDING DEMAND RISES Rising borrowing costs could push more companies away from public debt markets and toward private credit, according to executives at Bloomberg's Global Credit Forum. KKR warns that distressed debt ratios in U.S. and European leveraged loans and high-yield bonds could climb to 8%–9%, signaling mounting financial pressure. Meanwhile, HSBC identifies private credit as a major vulnerability, particularly loans issued to highly leveraged middle-market companies. Persistent rate hikes and AI-driven disruption could accelerate defaults, restructurings and broader credit-market stress.

text: DANSKE BANK ADDS THIRD FED RATE HIKE, SEES RATES AT 4.50%–4.75% BY MARCH 2027 Danske Bank has revised its Federal Reserve outlook, adding another rate increase to its forecast. The bank now expects three additional hikes, bringing the federal funds target range to 4.50%–4.75% by March 2027. Analysts cite growing inflation concerns among Fed policymakers, despite limited monetary policy guidance from Fed Chair Kevin Warsh. Danske expects stronger underlying economic growth to sustain inflationary pressures, forcing further tightening. The revised forecast reinforces expectations of higher borrowing costs for longer.

text: UKRAINIAN DRONE STRIKES SLASH RUSSIAN OIL REFINING BY 45%, THREATENING FUEL SUPPLIES Ukrainian drone attacks have reduced Russia's crude processing volumes by 45% since late October, according to industry estimates cited by Reuters. Operations at 15 of Russia's 35 major refineries have been disrupted or halted, up from nine last week. Daily refining volumes have fallen from over 700,000 metric tons to roughly 400,000 tons, equivalent to approximately 3 million barrels per day. The escalating strikes threaten to worsen Russian fuel shortages, constrain exports and tighten global diesel markets.

author: WalterBloomberg
text: U.S. PENDING HOME SALES PLUNGE 4.7%, MORE THAN DOUBLE EXPECTATIONS U.S. pending home sales fell 4.7% in October, sharply missing expectations for a 2.0% decline, according to the National Association of Realtors. The index dropped to 63.0, down from 66.1 in September, while sales plunged 16.7% year over year. Weakness extended across all four regions, with the West and South recording the steepest monthly declines. The disappointing figures signal continued deterioration in U.S. housing demand, as elevated mortgage rates and affordability pressures weigh on prospective buyers.

text: $ANT - ANTHROPIC IPO DRAWS NEARLY $500 BILLION IN ORDERS AS DEMAND EXPLODES Anthropic is considering expanding its IPO and pricing shares well above $80, CNBC reports. Institutional demand has reportedly reached $400 billion, with retail orders approaching $100 billion, although indications of interest are nonbinding. The company initially planned to raise up to $64.35 billion by selling 825 million shares. Anthropic reported $33.24 billion in nine-month revenue, up approximately 1,200%, with an October revenue run rate of $81 billion. Final pricing is expected Wednesday, ahead of Thursday's Nasdaq debut.

text: U.S. DEBT CEILING CRISIS LOOMS IN 2027 AS BORROWING APPROACHES $41.1 TRILLION LIMIT The U.S. government could hit its $41.1 trillion debt ceiling as early as February or March 2027, according to the Bipartisan Policy Center. Treasury cash reserves and extraordinary measures could delay a potential default until August–December 2027. With Congress divided, negotiations over raising the borrowing limit could trigger another political showdown. The looming deadline adds fiscal uncertainty and potential Treasury market volatility to existing concerns over rising interest rates and AI-sector valuations.

text: TRUMP GROWS FRUSTRATED WITH JD VANCE AS MARCO RUBIO GAINS FAVOR AHEAD OF 2028 President Trump has reportedly grown frustrated with Vice President JD Vance for blaming Republicans' midterm losses on the Iran war, according to The New York Times. Trump believes Vance should have explicitly defended the decision to attack Iran. Meanwhile, the president has privately praised Secretary of State Marco Rubio, fueling speculation about the 2028 Republican presidential nomination. Trump has also removed Vance from Iran peace negotiations. The tensions highlight growing uncertainty over Trump's preferred political successor.

text: GOLD, SILVER AND COPPER PLUNGE AS METALS SELLOFF ACCELERATES Precious and industrial metals extended losses, with futures falling to fresh lows for the year amid a stronger dollar and expectations of persistently high interest rates. text: U.S. 20-YEAR TREASURY AUCTION CLEARS AT 5.459% WITH SOLID DEMAND The U.S. Treasury sold $16 billion in 20-year bonds, with the auction clearing at a 5.459% yield, slightly below the previous auction's 5.469%. text: FED'S BARR BACKS FURTHER RATE HIKES AS INFLATION REMAINS TOO HIGH Federal Reserve Governor Michael Barr signaled support for additional interest-rate increases if the U.S. economy develops as expected. Barr warned that inflation remains too high, putting significant pressure on American households, and stressed the need to return inflation to the 2% target. He described the economy as strong, citing low unemployment, resilient consumer spending and robust business investment. Markets widely expect a 25-basis-point hike on December 9, bringing the federal funds target range to 4.00%–4.25%. His comments reinforce the Fed's increasingly hawkish policy outlook.
